newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie downtrend beckons as rally fails.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie downtrend beckons as rally fails.

text.p: *AUD in danger of entering fresh downtrend after breach of 74 cents confirmed last week's rally was merely a correction
*Bears encouraged by strong US economic data which raised risk of Fed hike, while policy bias here remains for easing
*$0.7365 support already tested this morning and analysts say longer term future to be decided at pivotal $0.7310/30 area
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the local dollar was languishing at US$0.7378/83 having slumped from US$0.7442/47 late Friday.
It had already probed US$0.7365 support in New Zealand time and analysts expected a grind down to the pivotal US$0.7310/30 area which marked 18-month lows a couple of weeks ago.

Bids had proved surprisingly robust on that occasion and dealers said they still had plenty of buy orders on the books for those prices. If this bulwark were to crack analysts looked for a quick move to US$0.7250 and then a steady retreat to the 1995 trough, and Fibonacci target, of US$0.7070/7100.
A recovery to US$0.7440 was needed to forestall the trend.
The poor tecnhical background was echoed by fundamentals, with yield differentials the most obvious negative.

Last week's 0.5 point cut to 5.0 percent left official rates below those in the U.S. for the first time since financial markets were deregulated in the early 1980s. And the deficit could yet widen further given the two economies were in very different stages of their cycles.

The pace of U.S. growth was illustrated by payrolls data and the Purchasing Management survey Friday which both surprise on the upside, while recent figures here including retail sales and building approvals have generally disappointed.

Private banking data suggested housing finance figures this Friday would also be weak, making the July labour report on Thursday all the more important. Anything less than the median forecast of 25,000 jobs growth would keep speculation of another easing alive and a fall would have the market baying for a cut.

Elsewhere, commodity prices had recovered somewhat recently with the Commodity Research Bureau index bouncing to 243.36 from a two-year low of 232.01 hit in early July but remained well short of the year's 254.79. The dollar was mixed on the crosses, being firm on the mark and Kiwi but off on the yen and Canadian dollar. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
